answer_cases.question: What relationship between context retrieval and agent memory is described by the corpus?

answer_cases.question: Does the corpus consistently describe an agent reviewing its own work as sufficient quality control?
required_claims: One source warns that self-review is only a second opinion from the same source.
Other material describes a separate grader or self-grader as part of an evaluation process.
The evidence treats self-review and independent evaluation as distinct arrangements rather than one practice.

evidence.snippet: your agent reviewing its own work is not a check. it is a second opinion from the same source. this is the most common gap in agent systems and it hides in plain sight, because the step exists. there is a review. it just cannot do the thing you think it does.

evidence.title: What is Claude Managed Agents?
evidence.snippet: A separate grader running at its own context window evaluates the output against my criteria. Claude reads that output and grades it independently.

The part of this setup nobody else is doing: the agent grades its own writing before it posts. Most AI content tools generate and stop. No quality bar, no feedback. In Sabrina’s build, the post-grader skill scored her own draft a 6.3.

answer_cases.question: What distinction does the corpus make between a task finishing successfully and a model simply running out of things to say?
answer_cases.retrieval_query: stop condition test passing file exists value matching
required_claims: A successful finish is tied to a stop condition such as a test passing, a file existing, or a value matching.

evidence.snippet: your agent did not finish the task. it ran out of things to say. these are different events and your trace records them identically. a run can end five ways. the stop condition was met. a test passed, a file exists, a value came back matching.

answer_cases.question: How does the corpus explain the difference between an agent harness and an agent loop?
answer_cases.retrieval_query: agent harness loops context engineering deterministic behavior
required_claims: The evidence names an agent harness, agent loops, and context engineering as topics a walkthrough covers.
The evidence is a list of topics and does not explain what distinguishes a harness from a loop, so the difference cannot be established from it.

evidence.snippet: Don't waste 2 years learning to build LLMs like Claude & ChatGPT. Thariq Shihipar shows you exactly how to build AI agents from scratch. • 00:00 - AI agent harness • 23:44 - building AI agent loops • 56:39 - AI agent context engineering • 1:33:34 - AI agent deterministic

answer_cases.review_rationale: The whole source is a 325-character post consisting of a chapter listing, so no enrichment is possible. A listing names topics but explains none of them; the prior SUPPORTED label asked the model to infer content from a table of contents, which caused a stable 0/3 failure under every prompt. Relabelled as a correct-refusal fixture and the question sharpened so the verdict follows from the evidence's nature, not from observed model behaviour.
forbidden_overclaims: The corpus explains how a harness differs from a loop.
The source provides a complete implementation of an agent harness.

answer_cases.question: What does the corpus describe as the purpose of evals for agent systems?

The corpus presents evals as part of improving an agent rather than as a one-time final check.

answer_cases.question: What does the corpus recommend considering when writing evaluations for an agent?
answer_cases.retrieval_query: how to write evaluations for agents
required_claims: An evaluation should be tied to the outcome or behavior the task is meant to produce.
Evaluation design should support repeated improvement rather than reward an isolated demonstration.
forbidden_overclaims: There is one universally correct evaluation design for all agents.
One source's evaluation practice is a universal rule for all agents.

evidence.title: Evaluating and improving Replit Agent at scale
evidence.snippet: The user expects to go from a prompt to a working application, but they don't tell us what kind of framework they want to use. They don't write tests. They just expect things to work after the agent run. [...] How do we track internally that the agent gets better on a daily basis and is actually aligned with what our users want? [...] Evaluations should highlight immediately what is breaking and inform us what we should be shipping next in terms of improvement for our agent. We're building a new system that allows us to do these constant improvements.

answer_cases.review_rationale: Evidence enriched from the source transcript: the original snippet supported repeated improvement but not the outcome-alignment claim, which caused a stable 0/3 failure under every prompt. Added the passage tying evaluation to what users actually want the agent to produce.

answer_cases.question: What lifecycle patterns does the corpus describe for agents that draft, evaluate, repair, and stop?
answer_cases.retrieval_query: agent loop draft evaluate repair stop
required_claims: The corpus describes a generator creating an initial draft and a separate evaluation identifying violations.
The corpus describes a repair step that uses those violations to make targeted fixes.
The corpus includes an explicit completion rule in which a loop processes one approved item and then stops.
forbidden_overclaims: Repeating a model call automatically makes the result reliable.

trajectory_cases.review_rationale: Asserts COMPLETED_AFTER_RETRY, the ordered stage sequence draft->evaluate->revise->draft->evaluate->finalize (gaps allowed for wrapper stages), and that the round-two prompt names the failed criterion. Order is asserted because a membership-only check survived a mutation that deleted the second draft/evaluate pair.
Asserts escalation rather than success, a bounded attempt count, and a persisted checkpoint.
Asserts FAILED_BUDGET with BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, recorded usage, no escalation label, and no call after the stop.

Asserts round one is not repeated, attempt history survives, and loop run_id is stable. KNOWN GAP: usage_preserved is not verified because validation-rejected attempts record no usage, so billed-but-rejected spend is lost on resume.
Asserts a single model call on first pass and cache reuse on the second run.
Asserts failed criteria, last output, evidence IDs, budget state, and a reviewer next action, both in memory and on disk.
Asserts a changed cache key and a fresh evaluation when task limits change; the schema variant covers output_schema_version.

repetition_policy.success_interpretation: A non-100% pass rate is acceptable only when failures are correctly classified, bounded, reproducible, and escalated with actionable diagnostics.

required_answer_evaluations.name: evidence_relevant
required_answer_evaluations.question: Does the retrieved evidence directly help answer the question?
required_answer_evaluations.pass_rule: Every material answer claim is addressed by at least one supplied evidence item.

required_answer_evaluations.name: claims_supported
required_answer_evaluations.question: Are the material claims supported by the supplied evidence without adding unsupported causal or numeric claims?
required_answer_evaluations.pass_rule: No material claim exceeds what the cited evidence establishes.

required_answer_evaluations.name: citations_valid
required_answer_evaluations.question: Do citations identify supplied evidence and support the nearby claim?
required_answer_evaluations.pass_rule: Every citation ID exists in the request and is relevant to the claim it supports.

required_answer_evaluations.name: answer_complete
required_answer_evaluations.question: Does the answer address every required part of the question?
required_answer_evaluations.pass_rule: All case-specific required claims, distinctions, and uncertainty labels are present.

optional_answer_evaluations.name: classification_calibrated
optional_answer_evaluations.pass_rule: SUPPORTED, INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE, and CONFLICTING_EVIDENCE match the case label.

optional_answer_evaluations.name: conflict_handled
optional_answer_evaluations.pass_rule: Material disagreement is surfaced rather than silently averaged or omitted, and absence-of-conflict claims remain scoped to the supplied retrieved evidence.

optional_answer_evaluations.name: source_diversity_acknowledged
optional_answer_evaluations.pass_rule: The answer distinguishes first-party, creator, and aggregator evidence when the case requires it.

optional_answer_evaluations.name: temporal_calibration
optional_answer_evaluations.pass_rule: The answer does not present dated or evolving claims as timeless facts.

optional_answer_evaluations.name: uncertainty_calibrated
optional_answer_evaluations.pass_rule: The answer distinguishes evidence, interpretation, opinion, and missing information.

trajectory_evaluations.name: retry_targets_failed_criterion
trajectory_evaluations.pass_rule: A revision addresses the failed evaluation criterion and is not merely an identical repeat.

trajectory_evaluations.name: stop_reason_valid
trajectory_evaluations.pass_rule: The recorded outcome and stop reason agree and are within configured limits.

trajectory_evaluations.name: checkpoint_resumable
trajectory_evaluations.pass_rule: Restarting resumes completed stages without repeating them or losing usage and attempt history.

trajectory_evaluations.name: escalation_actionable
trajectory_evaluations.pass_rule: Unresolved work includes failed criteria, last output, evidence IDs, budget state, and a next reviewer action.

trajectory_evaluations.name: cache_identity_safe
trajectory_evaluations.pass_rule: Changing question, evidence, prompt, model, evaluation policy, or task limits cannot reuse stale passing output.

operational_evaluations.name: cost_and_latency_recorded
operational_evaluations.pass_rule: Every completed model call records usage, estimated cost when known, and elapsed time.

operational_evaluations.name: repeated_run_consistency
operational_evaluations.pass_rule: Repeated runs report classification and stop behavior consistently, or expose the disagreement.

operational_evaluations.name: provider_comparison_fair
operational_evaluations.pass_rule: Compared providers receive identical questions, evidence, prompts, limits, and evaluation policy.
